title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ceramic ion conductor in which tin substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for preparing the same
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. The material comprises Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The zinc additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved dendrite suppression and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a ceramic ion conductor sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved sheet formability.

11. The method of claim 10, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.
12. The method of claim 10, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The silicon content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The silicon content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLTO, LLZO, and LATP material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 5 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material. The cell shows no short circuit for 300 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The suppression of void formation improves the interfacial resistance during fast charging.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. The Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF). Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF material. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing SiS2. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The content of SiS2 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The Li2ZrO3 and LATP material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. The mixed halogen substitution improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity of the all-solid-state battery.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which silver is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 500 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF). A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Tin-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 2 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and production method thereof
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF). The LiF material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a Li7P3S11 phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 5.5 mS/cm. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS material. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The ceramic ion conductor shows improved moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ion-conductive solid. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 50 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% over 100 cycles. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and ionic conductivity of the lithium metal battery.

title: Moisture-tolerant lithium indium chloride solid electrolyte with a surface fluorination layer and method of recovering conductivity after humid exposure
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises particles of Li3InCl6 having a monoclinic crystal structure and a surface fluorination layer having a thickness of 2 nm to 15 nm in which 20% to 60% of the chloride at the surface is replaced by fluoride. The fluorination layer is formed by exposing the chloride powder to a gas mixture containing 1 vol% to 5 vol% of fluorine in argon at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 10 minutes to 60 minutes. Because the fluoride is far less hygroscopic than the chloride, the water uptake of the powder at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% or less, and the ionic conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 70% or more of the initial value of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Even when the powder absorbs water to form a hydrate, the conductivity is recovered to 90% or more by vacuum drying at 150 degrees C to 200 degrees C, so that the powder can be handled in a dry room and processed into a slurry. A positive electrode mixture containing the electrolyte, stable up to 4.3 V versus Li/Li+, together with a sulfide glass ceramic shows improved high-voltage stability and moisture stability in production.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved moisture stability.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor with monoclinic structure for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor with monoclinic structure for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The resulting Li3YCl6 and LiF material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1.5 mA/cm2. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5% after 100 cycles. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium indium bromide solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide solid electrolyte in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, InBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 1.47 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved ionic conductivity and rate capability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1250 degrees C, and the resulting density is 96%. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The method gives reproducible densification and improved ionic conductivity at a lower cost.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film without any solvent. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The binder content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state lithium battery. The method shortens the process and improves the electrochemical window of the layer.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The material comprises Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for producing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The tin substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the sinterability in contact with lithium.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer that has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 15 micrometers. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiF and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 80% or more. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of indium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. In the trigonal structure, indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. A precursor of the Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with niobium and sintered with Li2CO3 is described. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The LLTO, LATP, and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The LLTO, LATP, and LLZO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. When v is 0.5, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.
claims: 1. 2. The method of claim 1, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.
3. The method of claim 1, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less.
4. The method of claim 1, wherein the reacting is performed for 6 hours to 72 hours.
5. The method of claim 1, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 9.4 wt% to 13.6 wt%.
6. The method of claim 1, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2 mS/cm or more.
7. The method of claim 1, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 380 degrees C to 430 degrees C.
8. An ion-conductive solid produced by the method of claim 1.
9. The ion-conductive solid of claim 8, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.
10. The ion-conductive solid of claim 8, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
11. The ion-conductive solid of claim 8, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a silicon-rich surface region is described. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.

4. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.
5. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.
6. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 5, wherein the substituting element is at least one selected from the group consisting of Sn, Sb, Si, and O.

7. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer comprises the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C has a thickness of 50 micrometers. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF, LLZO, and Li3YCl6 material. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl propionate to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.8 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

3. The sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C.
4. The sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.3 micrometers to 1 micrometers.
5. The sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 65% to 80%.
6. The sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.

7. A method for producing the sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and Li2O to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.
8. The method of claim 7, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
9. The method of claim 7, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The LiPON layer of 500 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the dendrite suppression and ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state battery is described. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. The oxygen substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the cycle life.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the cycle life.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. The additive content is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, the stack pressure is 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and the critical current density is 3 mA/cm2. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The lithium yttrium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance.

6. The positive electrode active material of claim 5, wherein a content of carbon in the material is 0.5 wt% or less.

8. The method of claim 7, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
9. The method of claim 7, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a beta-Li3PS4 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a lithium secondary battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability and cycle life.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% over 100 cycles. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.
