title: Germanium-substituted NASICON-type LATP ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The oxide particles have a core of the NASICON-type LATP phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved cycle life.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and method for producing the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 94% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The resulting Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLZO material. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the sinterability is improved.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Part of the titanium in the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved ionic conductivity at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte comprises a lithium metal layer, a solid electrolyte layer, and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 200 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF). The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LATP and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers, a porosity of 15%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved cycle life.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

11. The method of claim 10, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.
12. The method of claim 10, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.

A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A capacity retention of 90% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the cycle life.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A capacity retention of 90% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the cycle life.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with tantalum and sintered with Li2CO3 is described. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 5 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the grain boundary resistance of the garnet layer.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium zirconate and to a method for producing the same. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using acetonitrile and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. The material comprises Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The Li7P3S11 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.

title: Solvent-free self-supporting sulfide ion-conductive solid sheet bound by a fibrillated fluoropolymer network and method of forming the same
abstract: A self-supporting sheet comprises particles of an argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid of the Li6PS5Cl type and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 3 wt%, the binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without any solvent. The sheet is formed by kneading the powder and the binder under a shear rate of 200 s^-1 to 800 s^-1 at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C so that the binder is fibrillized, rolling the kneaded mass between a pair of rollers heated to 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and calendering the rolled film in at least three passes with a stepwise reduced roller gap to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 300 nm, and the sheet has a porosity of 8% or less, a tensile strength of 1.5 MPa or more, and an ionic conductivity of 2.0 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Because no polar solvent contacts the sulfide, the conductivity of the powder is retained, and the sheet can be wound on a roll and laminated onto an electrode without a drying step. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved sheet formability in production and improved cycle life.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). The lithium fluoride additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5% after 100 cycles. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing GeS2. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The content of GeS2 is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a gallium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 92% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1200 degrees C, and the resulting density is 95%. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability.

9. The garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the sintered body has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 500 micrometers.

A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and a gallium oxide with a lithium excess of 2 mol% to 10 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state lithium battery. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region for lithium battery
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The viscosity of 3000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the sheet formability and cycle life of the layer.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. In the orthorhombic structure, scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The LLZO material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which silver is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% to suppress dendrites. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The silver additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The additive content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, the stack pressure is 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and the critical current density is 1 mA/cm2. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The LiF and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3YCl6 and LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1.5 mA/cm2. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved dendrite suppression and cycle life.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). An ionic conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.1 to 1.5. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity of the lithium secondary battery.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 93% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1250 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm and a relative density of 96%. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the sinterability of the garnet layer.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 93% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1250 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm and a relative density of 96%. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the sinterability of the garnet layer.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12 and Al2O3 present at grain boundaries. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved sinterability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the grain boundary resistance are improved.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The resulting Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3YCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and cycle life and rate capability.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film without any solvent. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The LLZO and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers, a porosity of 10%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 85% or more. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The resulting Li3YCl6 and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% over 100 cycles. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.2 MPa or more. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 60 degrees C to form a continuous film. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The roll temperature is 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. The method shortens the process and improves the sinterability of the layer.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium metal layer, a ceramic ion conductor layer, and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7%. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the solid-state cell.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. When v is 0.2, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.6 mS/cm. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the sinterability is improved.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiTaO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance and rate capability.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which titanium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium chloride framework. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 60 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 30% or less. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and LiNbO3 material. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 97% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and production method thereof
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A precursor of the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material. The binder content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 3 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The Li6PS5Cl and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and LATP material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the interfacial resistance and sheet formability.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The solid content is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, the viscosity is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved cycle life.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of indium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved dendrite suppression.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window and moisture stability compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: A wet film of a solid electrolyte cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 15 micrometers. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the solid electrolyte, and the layer shows improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99% over 100 cycles. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described.
