title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The lithium niobate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with niobium and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The LLZO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% after 100 cycles. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life and dendrite suppression.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium scandium bromide solid electrolyte with trigonal structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide solid electrolyte in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The material comprises Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium scandium bromide solid electrolyte with trigonal structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide solid electrolyte in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The material comprises Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3InCl6 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The high coverage of the coating results in improved ionic conductivity at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. A precursor of the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability of the layer.

10. The method of claim 9, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.
11. The method of claim 10, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the cycle life of the cell.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the cycle life of the cell.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. A solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The low electronic conductivity of the LiNbO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The lithium tungstate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with trigonal structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability and high-voltage stability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The sheet thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, the porosity is 10% or less, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 material. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12 and Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries. The LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a beta-Li3PS4 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 2 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The low electronic conductivity of the Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and LiF material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The material comprises Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder for lithium battery
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The LATP, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The binder content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa and a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the cycle life and sheet formability.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 50 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% over 100 cycles. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the ionic conductivity.

5. The garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.6 micrometers to 2 micrometers.

6. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and a tantalum oxide with a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.
7. The method of claim 6, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.
8. The method of claim 6, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2WO4 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which zinc is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% to suppress dendrites. The Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The zinc additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The critical current density is 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved high-voltage stability and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window of the solid-state battery.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 300 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% over 100 cycles. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the cycle life and dendrite suppression.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on NASICON-type LATP and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.5 V. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity and sinterability of the electrolyte layer.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for producing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.045 or less. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability and cycle life of the all-solid-state battery.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP material. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Sintering at 1150 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 97% and a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the high-voltage stability.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 91% or more after sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm and a relative density of 95%. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing GeS2. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The content of GeS2 is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6 material. The Al2O3 layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The Al2O3 layer of 500 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the cycle life.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. With hafnium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The content of SiS2 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The oxygen substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. The resulting Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the lithium metal battery.
