title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which solid electrolyte particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7P3S11. A sheet of 20 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life of the cell.

6. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.
7. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm.

8. A method for producing the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the solid electrolyte powder with 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers.
9. The method of claim 8, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.

A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the lithium secondary battery. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

2. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
3. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the coating layer comprises at least one selected from the group consisting of LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, LiTaO3, Li2WO4, Li3BO3, and Li3InCl6.
4. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the core particles are secondary particles having an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers.
5. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, further comprising a binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt%.
6. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 66% or more.
7. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the coating layer is amorphous as confirmed by transmission electron microscopy.

8. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises the positive electrode active material of claim 1.
9. The lithium secondary battery of claim 8, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers to 100 micrometers.
10. The lithium secondary battery of claim 8, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.
11. The lithium secondary battery of claim 8, wherein the battery is a laminate cell comprising at least two unit cells stacked in series.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

7. The moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein an electronic conductivity of the material at 25 degrees C is 1 x 10^-8 S/cm or less.

12. The method of claim 10, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A precursor of the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The sintered body has a relative density of 92%, an average grain size of 8 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO, LATP, and Li2ZrO3 material. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The method gives reproducible densification and improved high-voltage stability at a lower cost.

title: Tin-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.5 V and production method thereof
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability of the electrolyte layer.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by sputtering
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising an Ag-C inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLTO, LATP, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 85%. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLTO, LATP, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 85%. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 80% after humid exposure. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which silver is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The critical current density is 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the moisture stability is retained.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. An ionic conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.1 to 0.55. A precursor of the Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which zinc is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium fluoride (LiF). A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and the critical current density is 4 mA/cm2. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.15 or less. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LiF material. Specific examples are Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The material comprises Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The bilayer structure improves the cycle life compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability.

A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and production method thereof
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The content of LiI is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

8. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the glass transition temperature of the glass phase is 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The oxygen content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability and rate capability.

6. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.
7. The positive electrode active material of claim 6, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
8. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

9. A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.
10. The method of claim 9, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.
11. The method of claim 10, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.

An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises the positive electrode active material of claim 1.
13. The all-solid-state battery of claim 12, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 85%. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The silicon substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The wet film is dried at 100 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state lithium battery is described. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a solid-state lithium battery including the sheet are described. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium battery is described. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor in which tin substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.5 V. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and production method thereof
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The LGPS and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved sheet formability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The oxygen content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the moisture stability is improved.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of scandium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, ScBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In the trigonal structure, scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with an indium additive. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The critical current density is 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The indium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved dendrite suppression.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing LiI. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. An ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which titanium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium bromide framework. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and high-voltage stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The LGPS and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer comprises solid electrolyte particles, a styrene-butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent butyl butyrate. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The viscosity of 500 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the cycle life of the cell.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. In the orthorhombic structure, scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A wet film of a solid electrolyte cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
