title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The oxidation potential is 5 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 5 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO and LATP material. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The oxide particles have a core of the NASICON-type LATP phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in zirconium. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 90%. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The LLTO, LLZO, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3%. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6 and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 2 mA/cm2. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the interfacial resistance.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The inorganic layer has a thickness of 100 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% over 100 cycles. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.
claims: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.9 mS/cm or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The LiF layer of 200 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 3.1 mS/cm. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved dendrite suppression.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The viscosity of 1000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. When z is 0.3, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. The Li3InCl6 and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life and sheet formability.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. After dehydration under vacuum at 350 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and rate capability.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 89% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. When v is 0.3, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the sinterability is improved.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 250 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and LiNbO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and LiNbO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state battery using it. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 30% to 65% by X-ray diffraction. The Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 80% or more. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Part of the titanium in the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved electrochemical window.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state lithium battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The LLZO, LiF, and Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% after 100 cycles. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life of the lithium metal battery.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. A solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved interfacial resistance and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium battery is described. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better interfacial resistance.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better interfacial resistance.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The silver additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The critical current density is 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity of the solid-state cell.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2WO4 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 96% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The sintered body has a relative density of 96%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.12 or less. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.1 to 1.5. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 10 mol%. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A precursor of the LLTO, LATP, and Li2ZrO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Br6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which zirconium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium bromide framework. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

2. The method of claim 1, wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C.
3. The method of claim 1, wherein the reacting is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more.
4. The method of claim 1, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.7 mS/cm or more.
5. The method of claim 1, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.4 wt% or less.
6. The method of claim 1, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less.
7. The method of claim 1, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.
8. The method of claim 1, wherein the reaction temperature is 75 degrees C to 90 degrees C.
9. The method of claim 8, wherein a carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.5 wt% or less.
10. The method of claim 1, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more.
11. The method of claim 1, wherein the suspension further contains LiCl dissolved therein.
12. The method of claim 1, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 530 degrees C to 580 degrees C.
13. The method of claim 12, wherein the precipitate is separated by filtration before the removing of the solvent.
14. The method of claim 1, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 200 degrees C.
15. An ion-conductive solid produced by the method of claim 1.
16. The ion-conductive solid of claim 15, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.
17. The ion-conductive solid of claim 15, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
18. The ion-conductive solid of claim 15, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.

19. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer comprises the ion-conductive solid of claim 15.
20. The all-solid-state battery of claim 19, wherein the positive electrode layer further comprises a conductive carbon in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt%.
21. The all-solid-state battery of claim 19, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.
22. The all-solid-state battery of claim 21, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.
claims: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.
2. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material has a water content of 0.5 wt% or less as measured by Karl Fischer titration.
3. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the content of SiS2 is 7.5 mol% to 10.9 mol%.
4. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.
5. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more.
6. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein an electronic conductivity of the material at 25 degrees C is 1 x 10^-8 S/cm or less.
7. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 55% to 70%.
8. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein a particle size distribution of the material has a D90 of 20 micrometers or less.
9. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 8, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.
10. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 9, wherein the material is stored in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
11. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the glass phase further contains at least one selected from the group consisting of GeS2, SiS2, LiI, Li2O, and P2O5.

12. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and SiS2 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.
13. The method of claim 12, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.
14. The method of claim 13, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.
15. The method of claim 12, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.

16. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer comprises the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1.
17. The lithium secondary battery of claim 16, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.
18. The lithium secondary battery of claim 16, wherein the battery is pressed at a pressure of 1 MPa to 20 MPa during operation.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The LGPS material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A capacity retention of 90% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the sinterability.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. When v is 0.25, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.6 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
