title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The Ag-C layer of 300 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved dendrite suppression and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. An all-solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 2 MPa. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity of the solid-state cell.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 5.5 mS/cm. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 5.5 mS/cm. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The content of LiI is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. After dehydration under vacuum at 350 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. An H2S generation of 4 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The oxygen substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The LLZO and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. A precursor of the LATP and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 15 micrometers. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. The resulting Li7P3S11 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The material comprises Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. With a binder content of 3 wt% and a roll temperature of 120 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 20% or less. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The LATP and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved high-voltage stability and rate performance.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The oxidation potential is 5 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and production method thereof
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 96% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The tin substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The additive content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, the stack pressure is 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and the critical current density is 1 mA/cm2. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and beta-Li3PS4. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The method prevents short circuit and improves the ionic conductivity without a thick protective layer.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium indium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl and LiNbO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3YCl6. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 94% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 8 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved moisture stability.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 94% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 8 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved moisture stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 material. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 5.5 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The ion-conductive solid shows improved moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Niobium-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and lithium battery
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12 and Al2O3 present at grain boundaries. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 96% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The low electronic conductivity of the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and cycle life.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The method prevents short circuit and improves the cycle life without a thick protective layer.
claims: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more.
2. The negative electrode structure of claim 1, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
3. The negative electrode structure of claim 1, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.
4. The negative electrode structure of claim 1, further comprising a binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt%.

5. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises the negative electrode structure of claim 1.
6. The all-solid-state battery of claim 5, wherein the battery is a laminate cell comprising at least two unit cells stacked in series.
7. The all-solid-state battery of claim 6, further comprising an intermediate layer disposed between the negative electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ion-conductive solid provides improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6, LiF, Li3InCl6, and LiNbO3 material. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% after 100 cycles. The LLZO, Li3YCl6, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life and dendrite suppression.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6 and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which hafnium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium bromide framework. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, ErBr3, and HfBr4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the electrochemical window.
claims: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more.
2. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers.
3. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more.
4. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.
5. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

6. A method for producing the halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing LiBr, ErBr3, and HfBr4 in a molar ratio corresponding to the composition; mechanochemically reacting the mixture in a sealed container; and heat-treating the reacted powder at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C under an inert atmosphere.
7. The method of claim 6, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

8. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer comprises the halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and production method thereof
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. In the trigonal structure, yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the high-voltage stability and moisture stability.

6. The all-solid-state battery of claim 5, further comprising a buffer layer disposed between the negative electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.

6. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein an anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles has a thickness of 10 nm or less.
7. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more.

8. 9. The method of claim 8, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
10. The method of claim 8, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.

11. title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with niobium and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 89% or more after sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.

11. The garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Gallium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with gallium and sintered with LiF is described. The resulting LATP material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. When v is 0.3, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The dopant gallium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.15 to 0.5, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the lithium secondary battery. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved cycle life.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1.5 mA/cm2. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the interfacial resistance.

title: Germanium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V and production method thereof
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. With germanium substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The germanium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the cycle life and electrochemical window in contact with lithium.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more and a critical current density of 3 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The magnesium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the solid-state cell.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.6 MPa or more. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The binder content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The method shortens the process and improves the electrochemical window and interfacial resistance of the layer.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

3. The method of claim 1, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 20 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7%. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance.
