title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium metal layer, a ceramic ion conductor layer, and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. A Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more and a critical current density of 4 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The zinc additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which zinc is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% to suppress dendrites. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. A Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more and a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.12 or less. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability.

title: Zirconium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor stable above 5 V and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A capacity retention of 92% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and method for producing the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers after calendering. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life of the layer.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and method for producing the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers after calendering. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life of the layer.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. With zirconium substitution of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the lithium secondary battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The ion-conductive solid shows improved moisture stability and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The content of LiI is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability and cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF). A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The roll temperature is 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers after calendering. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the sheet formability of the cell.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance.
claims: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 65% or more.
2. The moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein an electronic conductivity of the material at 25 degrees C is 1 x 10^-8 S/cm or less.

3. The moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 3 mol%.
4. The moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, further comprising a binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt%.
5. The moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 390 degrees C to 420 degrees C.
6. The moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 2 cm3/g or less.
7. The moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the hydrolysis of the sulfide is suppressed such that the pH of water in contact with the powder remains 10 or less.
8. The moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers.
9. The moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the H2S generation is measured by a hydrogen sulfide sensor in a sealed chamber of 1 L at 25 degrees C.
10. The moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein a content of carbon in the material is 0.5 wt% or less.
11. The moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the material has a water content of 0.5 wt% or less as measured by Karl Fischer titration.

12. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and an arsenic-free antimony source at a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.
13. The method of claim 12, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
14. The method of claim 12, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.
15. The method of claim 12, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

16. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1.
17. The lithium secondary battery of claim 16, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.
18. The lithium secondary battery of claim 17, wherein the positive electrode layer further comprises a conductive carbon in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.

title: Zirconium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The LLTO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.5 V. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The resulting Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3BO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The lithium borate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from acetonitrile, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers, a porosity of 10%, a tensile strength of 2 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity and sheet formability of the cell.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.3 to 1.7. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. A Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more and a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO, Li3YCl6, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. An all-solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance during fast charging.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers after calendering. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and lithium battery
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12 and Al2O3 present at grain boundaries. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The method gives reproducible densification and improved ionic conductivity at a lower cost.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The tin substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.

8. The method of claim 7, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.

9. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The solvent is ethyl propionate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved grain boundary resistance.

The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using 1,2-dimethoxyethane and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm. A precursor of the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The oxygen substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.

title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising an Ag-C inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved moisture stability.
claims: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers.
2. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 258 nm to 402 nm.
3. The protective layer of claim 2, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
4. The protective layer of claim 3, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.
5. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein an electronic conductivity of the material at 25 degrees C is 1 x 10^-8 S/cm or less.
6. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the inorganic layer is amorphous.
7. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1.04 micrometers to 1.76 micrometers.
8. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the wettability of molten lithium on the protective layer has a contact angle of 30 degrees or less.
9. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.6 micrometers to 2 micrometers.
10. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 99.5% or more.

11. A method for producing the protective layer of claim 1, the method comprising: forming the inorganic layer on the lithium metal by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm; applying a solution containing a fluorine-containing polymer and a lithium salt onto the inorganic layer; and drying the applied solution to form the polymer layer.
12. The method of claim 11, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
13. The method of claim 12, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
14. The method of claim 11, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.

15. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the protective layer of claim 1.
16. The solid-state battery of claim 15, wherein the solid electrolyte layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers to 100 micrometers.
17. The solid-state battery of claim 15, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a zinc additive. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF material. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1 mA/cm2. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF). The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which solid electrolyte particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved interfacial resistance.

5. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the sheet is laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step.
6. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 2.2 MPa or more.
7. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 1.2 micrometers to 4 micrometers.
8. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the material has an activation energy for lithium ion conduction of 0.40 eV or less.
9. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 14 micrometers to 30 micrometers.

10. A method for producing the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the solid electrolyte powder with 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers.
11. The method of claim 10, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
12. The method of claim 11, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.
13. The method of claim 10, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.

16. The solid-state lithium battery of claim 14, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the cycle life of the cell.

3. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the crystal phase has an average crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm.
4. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, further comprising a binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt%.
5. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.
6. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the content of SiS2 is 4.7 mol% to 6.8 mol%.
7. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.
8. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 305 degrees C to 340 degrees C.
9. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours.

10. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and SiS2 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.
11. The method of claim 10, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
12. The method of claim 10, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The resulting Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li2ZrO3 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ion-conductive solid film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The material comprises Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 120 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 20% or less. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved high-voltage stability and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li3YCl6 material. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the dendrite suppression is improved.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3YCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Firing is performed at 550 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A precursor of the Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Hafnium-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and method for producing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The LATP and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The oxide particles have a core of the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life of the layer.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
