title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1 mA/cm2. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the dendrite suppression.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An ionic conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.045 or less. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air for lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. An all-solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The silicon substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 120 degrees C to form a continuous film. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The sheet thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, the porosity is 16% or less, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved sheet formability.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tungsten and sintered with LiF is described. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. When v is 0.2, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer that has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the layer shows improved ionic conductivity and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state battery is described. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the solid-state lithium battery.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12 and Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The sintered body has a relative density of 96%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A sheet of 30 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life of the cell.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and LiF material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl propionate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl propionate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.

title: Tin-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid stable above 5 V and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Al2O3 layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ion-conductive solid. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved electrochemical window and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Al2O3 layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ion-conductive solid. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved electrochemical window and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl acetate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The ion-conductive solid shows improved cycle life and moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state lithium battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The lithium tungstate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3 and LiF material. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium fluoride (LiF). Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A wet film of an ion-conductive solid cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The wet film is dried at 120 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved interfacial resistance and sheet formability.
claims: 1. A method for producing the slurry of claim 1, the method comprising: applying the slurry having a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% onto a release film by a doctor blade; drying the applied slurry at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C in an oven; and peeling the dried layer from the release film and pressing it onto an electrode.
12. The method of claim 11, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.

14. The method of claim 13, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting solid electrolyte film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved ionic conductivity.

2. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the binder is at least one selected from the group consisting of PTFE, a PTFE copolymer, and ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene.

7. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm.
8. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 3.3 MPa or more.
9. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 90 degrees C.
10. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers.
11. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1.
12. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 4, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 43 micrometers to 67 micrometers.

A method for producing the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the solid electrolyte powder with 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance and rate capability.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO solid electrolyte in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 5 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on phosphate-based NASICON and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP material. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 85%. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 3 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li6PS5Cl, and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved cycle life and dendrite suppression.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 92%. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer that has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance of the layer.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). When v is 0.3, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.6 mS/cm. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The resulting Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3%. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The lithium fluoride additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 0.84 mS/cm or more. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved ionic conductivity and simpler handling.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium scandium bromide ceramic ion conductor with monoclinic structure and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, ScBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium scandium bromide ceramic ion conductor with monoclinic structure and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, ScBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF). A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state battery. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by sputtering. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. The LiPON layer of 300 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life of the lithium metal battery.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide ion-conductive solid in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6 material. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved moisture stability.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the cycle life of the cell.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the cycle life of the cell.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.6 mS/cm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the sinterability of the garnet layer.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium yttrium chloride and to a method for producing the same. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The resulting Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.
