title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a lithium fluoride additive. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 4 mA/cm2. The Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity of the solid-state cell.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. An H2S generation of 4 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and simpler handling.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 10 MPa. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in acetonitrile at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The Li3PS4 and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a silver-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 10 MPa. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the dendrite suppression.

abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The content of Li2O is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
claims: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours.
2. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the material has an activation energy for lithium ion conduction of 0.40 eV or less.
3. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein devitrification to a Li4P2S6 phase is 5% or less by weight.
4. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 1.5 micrometers to 15 micrometers.
5. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers to 10 micrometers.
6. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein a content of carbon in the material is 0.5 wt% or less.
7. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 75% to 90%.
8. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the glass phase further contains at least one selected from the group consisting of GeS2, SiS2, LiI, Li2O, and P2O5.
9. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 312 degrees C to 333 degrees C.

10. A method for producing the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and Li2O to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.
11. The method of claim 10, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.
12. The method of claim 10, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.

13. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1.
14. The all-solid-state battery of claim 13, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.
15. The all-solid-state battery of claim 13, wherein the solid electrolyte layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP, Li3PS4, and LLZO material. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers, a porosity of 8%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 120 degrees C to form a continuous film. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. A solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte shows improved cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Zirconium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. With zirconium substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitated from ethyl propionate and solid electrolyte produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S, P2S5, and LiCl in ethyl propionate at a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 15 wt% to form a suspension, stirring the suspension at 40 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 12 hours to 48 hours so that a solvate complex of Li3PS4 and LiCl precipitates, separating the precipitate by filtration, removing the solvent at 150 degrees C to 190 degrees C under a pressure of 1 kPa or less, and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 430 degrees C to 480 degrees C in argon to crystallize an argyrodite phase. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the particles are formed by precipitation and have a narrow size distribution with a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 2 micrometers, and no long mechanical milling is required. The residual solvent content after drying is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.2 wt% or less, so that the grain boundary resistance of a pressed pellet is 15% or less of the total resistance. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The method is suitable for mass production of Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 type solid electrolytes.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Zirconium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 4.5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. A capacity retention of 90% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. A precursor of the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 5.5 mS/cm. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.
claims: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%.
2. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 272 degrees C to 293 degrees C.
3. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 2, wherein the activation energy for lithium ion conduction is 0.25 eV or less.
4. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 3, wherein the crystal phase has an average crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm.
5. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 1 hours to 4 hours.

6. A method for producing the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and P2O5 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.
7. The method of claim 6, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.
8. The method of claim 6, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.

9. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1.
10. The solid-state battery of claim 9, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6 and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better grain boundary resistance.
claims: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more.
2. The halide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.
3. The halide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more.
4. The halide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein 0.09 <= z <= 0.13.
5. The halide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more.

6. A method for producing the halide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing LiBr, YBr3, and ZrBr4 in a molar ratio corresponding to the composition; mechanochemically reacting the mixture in a sealed container; and heat-treating the reacted powder at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C under an inert atmosphere.
7. The method of claim 6, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
8. The method of claim 7, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.

9. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises the halide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1.
10. The all-solid-state battery of claim 9, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3YCl6. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

10. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.89 mS/cm or more.

22. The all-solid-state battery of claim 20, wherein the battery is a laminate cell comprising at least two unit cells stacked in series.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3YCl6. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. An ionic conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on perovskite-type LLTO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The Li6PS5Cl and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using acetonitrile for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.

15. The method of claim 1, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

17. The method of claim 1, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ceramic ion conductor particles are dispersed in anisole with a rubber binder and a dispersant. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 30 micrometers. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ceramic ion conductor, and the layer shows improved cycle life and sheet formability.

2. The slurry of claim 1, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
3. The slurry of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.
4. The slurry of claim 1, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 2.58 wt% to 4.02 wt%.
5. The slurry of claim 1, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 37 wt% to 43 wt%.
6. The slurry of claim 1, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.
7. The slurry of claim 6, wherein the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%.
8. The slurry of claim 1, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s.

9. A method for producing the slurry of claim 1, the method comprising: applying the slurry having a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% onto a release film by a doctor blade; drying the applied slurry at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C in an oven; and peeling the dried layer from the release film and pressing it onto an electrode.
10. The method of claim 9, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.
11. The method of claim 9, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.

12. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises the slurry of claim 1.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming an ion-conductive solid layer. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The viscosity of 2000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The wet film is dried at 120 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved sheet formability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. A solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 94% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The LLZO, LLTO, and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A precursor of the LLZO, LLTO, and LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The grain size is 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and the relative density is 94% or more after sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability.

title: Tin-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide solid electrolyte stable above 5 V and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide solid electrolyte in which tin substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved sinterability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% and no dendrite penetration is observed. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. The bilayer structure improves the moisture stability compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. When v is 0.2, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.6 mS/cm. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, LLTO, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The dopant gallium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.35 mS/cm or more. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl propionate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3PS4 and LLZO material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved moisture stability.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which titanium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium chloride framework. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF). The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The oxygen substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 5 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 5 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 91% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. When v is 0.2, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The total ionic conductivity is 0.42 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.2 to 1.6. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tantalum and sintered with Al2O3 is described. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1150 degrees C, and the resulting density is 94%. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using tetrahydrofuran and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved dendrite suppression and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium borate and to a method for producing the same. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The lithium borate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ceramic ion conductor in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. In the orthorhombic structure, scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.
