title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The LLZO and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and sinterability.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A precursor of the Li3PS4 and LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. The Li3PS4 and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The oxygen substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNbO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium fluoride (LiF). The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 5.5 mS/cm. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The material comprises Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.

title: Zirconium-substituted NASICON-type LATP solid electrolyte stable above 5 V for lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The LLTO, LLZO, and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The content of LiI is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the interfacial resistance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium battery is described. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and high-voltage stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium battery is described. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved ionic conductivity and simpler handling.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the moisture stability.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved dendrite suppression.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl acetate for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. After heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 5.5 mS/cm. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the lithium secondary battery. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved moisture stability and rate capability.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The protective layer thickness is 120 nm to 600 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li3YCl6, and beta-Li3PS4. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved cycle life and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and method for preparing the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by solution casting followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved high-voltage stability and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.

5. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.
6. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 5, wherein the H2S generation is measured by a hydrogen sulfide sensor in a sealed chamber of 1 L at 25 degrees C.

7. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and an arsenic-free antimony source at a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.
8. The method of claim 7, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
9. The method of claim 8, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

10. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer comprises the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1.
11. The solid-state battery of claim 10, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.
12. The solid-state battery of claim 10, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ceramic ion conductor in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 50 nm. The protective layer thickness is 20 nm to 100 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.3% or more. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ion-conductive solid. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The critical current density is 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more. The suppression of void formation improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity during fast charging.

abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ion-conductive solid. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The critical current density is 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more. The suppression of void formation improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity during fast charging.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the solid-state cell.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with an indium additive. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 1 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 200 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life of the solid-state cell.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An H2S generation of 4 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The resulting Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.
claims: 1. 2. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, further comprising a binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt%.
3. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 99% or more.
4. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity.

5. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer comprises the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1.
6. The all-solid-state battery of claim 5, further comprising a buffer layer disposed between the negative electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The low electronic conductivity of the Li2ZrO3 and LiNbO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from 1,2-dimethoxyethane, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 1 wt%. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium bromide ceramic ion conductor with monoclinic structure and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium bromide framework. The LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and high-voltage stability.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium bromide ceramic ion conductor with monoclinic structure and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium bromide framework. The LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state battery is described. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3YCl6. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state battery. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3YCl6 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.1 to 0.45, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The viscosity of 500 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved ionic conductivity and sheet formability.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The viscosity of 500 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved ionic conductivity and sheet formability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. The LiF, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The bilayer structure improves the ionic conductivity compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 5 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The dopant tantalum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and to a method of handling it in a dry room. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The tin substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability and moisture stability.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The LLZO, LATP, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The sintered body has a relative density of 95%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which zirconium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.02 to 0.25. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiTaO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the sheet formability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. The LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The content of P2O5 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with a zinc additive. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3YCl6 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 3 mA/cm2. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The low electronic conductivity of the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a silicon-rich surface region is described. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing SiS2. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 3 mA/cm2. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF and Li3YCl6 material. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.

title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A precursor of the Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. The Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 2 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 500 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the sheet formability is improved.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A solid-state battery comprising the LLTO and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The material comprises Li3InCl6, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The Li3InCl6, Li6PS5Cl, and LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li3YCl6. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. An ionic conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.1 to 1.5. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.075 or less. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved dendrite suppression and interfacial resistance.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering an aluminum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 92% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The Li2ZrO3 and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 5 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The Li2ZrO3 and LLTO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
