title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The resulting LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.

abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.

title: Ceramic ion conductor slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A wet film of a ceramic ion conductor cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C in an oven. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved sheet formability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12 and Al2O3 present at grain boundaries. When v is 0.3, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. The LATP, LLZO, and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state lithium battery using it. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The silicon substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The silicon substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. A precursor of the Li3PS4 and LiF material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and LiF material. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The bilayer structure improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: High-conductivity argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor with a lithium-deficient composition and an impurity-free diffraction pattern
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a lithium-deficient composition represented by Li(6-x-y)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.5 and 0 < y <= 0.15, the lithium deficiency y being introduced by adding P2S5 in a slight excess so that lithium vacancies are created on the 48h site. The anion disorder between the sulfur and chlorine sites is 40% or more, no diffraction peak attributable to LiCl, Li3PS4, or Li2S is observed, and the lattice parameter is 9.80 angstroms to 9.86 angstroms. The combination of the vacancies and the anion disorder gives an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C for a cold-pressed pellet and 9 mS/cm or more for a pellet sintered at 500 degrees C, together with an activation energy of 0.26 eV or less. The material is crystalline and is not a glass ceramic, so that its conductivity does not decrease upon storage at 60 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor widens the electrochemical window of a positive electrode mixture compared with Li10GeP2S12 and Li7P3S11, and an all-solid-state battery using the material in the separator layer and the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability.

8. The sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein a decrease in ionic conductivity after storage at 60 degrees C for 30 days in argon is 5% or less.
9. A positive electrode mixture comprising a positive electrode active material coated with lithium niobate and the sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1.

10. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer comprising the positive electrode mixture of claim 9, a negative electrode layer, and a separator layer comprising the sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1.

11. A method of manufacturing the sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and LiCl such that P2S5 is in excess by 1 mol% to 5 mol% relative to the stoichiometric composition; mechanically milling the mixture; and firing the milled mixture at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an inert gas atmosphere.
12. The method of claim 11, wherein the firing is performed for 4 hours to 12 hours.
13. The method of claim 11, wherein the mechanical milling is performed in a planetary mill at 400 rpm to 600 rpm.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. The LGPS material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An all-solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and rate capability.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which solid electrolyte particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The tensile strength is 0.6 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the moisture stability and cycle life of the cell.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. With zirconium substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.

10. The method of claim 9, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.
11. The method of claim 9, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium scandium bromide ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium scandium bromide ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.2 mS/cm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for producing the same
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The grain size is 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and the relative density is 89% or more after sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The method gives reproducible densification and improved high-voltage stability at a lower cost.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. The Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and LiNbO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.

11. The method of claim 7, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which indium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. The critical current density is 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6. The method prevents short circuit and improves the dendrite suppression and ionic conductivity without a thick protective layer.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The content of SiS2 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LGPS material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium bromide ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, ScBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ion-conductive solid in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. In the orthorhombic structure, erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The LiF and Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. A precursor of the LiF and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF). The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An ionic conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.2 to 1.6. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and cycle life.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. The binder content is 1 wt%, the drying temperature is 120 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.15 or less. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a magnesium-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 2 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 1000 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The resulting Li3YCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a lithium fluoride-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 2 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 1000 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The LiF, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 4.2 mS/cm. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP material. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The method gives reproducible densification and improved ionic conductivity at a lower cost.

title: Gallium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12 and Al2O3 present at grain boundaries. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The LLZO and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The dopant gallium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1250 degrees C, and the resulting density is 92%. The Li2ZrO3 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.15 or less. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state lithium battery. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The ion-conductive solid shows improved cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl propionate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl propionate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm and a relative density of 92%. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid shows improved ionic conductivity and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on phosphate-based NASICON and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 75% or more. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The LATP and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ion-conductive solid at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ion-conductive solid at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.

2. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the inorganic layer is amorphous.
3. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide.
4. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the inorganic layer has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C.
5. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 43 nm to 67 nm.
6. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.45 micrometers to 4.5 micrometers.
7. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.

8. A method for producing the protective layer of claim 1, the method comprising: forming the inorganic layer on the lithium metal by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm; applying a solution containing a fluorine-containing polymer and a lithium salt onto the inorganic layer; and drying the applied solution to form the polymer layer.
9. The method of claim 8, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

10. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises the protective layer of claim 1.
11. The all-solid-state battery of claim 10, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

4. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the material is stored in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
5. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.
6. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C.
7. The positive electrode active material of claim 6, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.
8. The positive electrode active material of claim 7, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.
9. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein a content of carbon in the material is 0.5 wt% or less.
10. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm.

11. A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.
12. The method of claim 11, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
13. The method of claim 12, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.
14. The method of claim 11, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
