title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1100 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 96%. The method gives reproducible densification and improved sinterability at a lower cost.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing LiI. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability and cycle life.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the solid-state battery. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the sinterability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The resulting Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and high-voltage stability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm is provided. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The average thickness of the coating is 4 nm to 20 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The Li2ZrO3, LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and cycle life and rate capability.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which titanium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium bromide framework. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. After dehydration under vacuum at 350 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. The Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved moisture stability and rate capability.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved sinterability and ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3YCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3YCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The lithium yttrium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl propionate for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The Li7P3S11 and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and LiNbO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. A capacity retention of 92% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3InCl6. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 for lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, InCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. In the trigonal structure, indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The Li3InCl6, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and high-voltage stability.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. Part of the titanium in the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The content of GeS2 is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved moisture stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.

abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl propionate to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl acetate to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a zinc-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. With the additive in an amount of 1 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7%. The zinc additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet having a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and a porosity of 30% or less is provided. With a binder content of 3 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 30% or less. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a niobium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 92% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLTO material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of indium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of indium and zirconium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.5 V. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The material comprises Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The oxygen substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The bilayer structure improves the ionic conductivity compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability and moisture stability.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiF inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The bilayer structure improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiF inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 100 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% over 100 cycles. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The material comprises Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. In the trigonal structure, scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The Li3YCl6 and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with niobium and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LATP and LLTO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. When v is 0.5, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa with a zinc additive. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3YCl6 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 1000 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. An ionic conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.2 to 1.6. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from 1,2-dimethoxyethane, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The method gives reproducible densification and improved high-voltage stability at a lower cost.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming an ion-conductive solid sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in acetonitrile to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The magnesium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 300 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the dendrite suppression is improved.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and method for producing the same
abstract: A method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The slurry has a solid content of 70 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The LLZO and LATP material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The suspension has a solid concentration of 4 wt% to 16 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved moisture stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The LATP, LLZO, and LLTO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The oxygen content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 2.2 mS/cm or more. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability and simpler handling.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The oxygen content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 2.2 mS/cm or more. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability and simpler handling.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The tin content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS material. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The lithium borate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.
