title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the sinterability is improved.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting solid electrolyte film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The LATP, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting solid electrolyte film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The LATP, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with an indium additive. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1.5 mA/cm2. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 10 mol%. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The material comprises Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The lithium niobate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the moisture stability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The LiF and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 10 MPa. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. The LiF and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the solid-state cell.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and LiF material. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the lithium metal battery.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability and high-voltage stability of the electrolyte layer.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A precursor of the Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The Li3InCl6 and LiF material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium zirconate and to a method for producing the same. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3 and Li6PS5Cl material. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.

The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The LATP, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C has a thickness of 15 micrometers. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the sheet formability of the layer.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. A precursor of the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity of the solid-state battery.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The content of SiS2 is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with aluminum and sintered with Al2O3 is described. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.1 to 0.45, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The total ionic conductivity is 0.28 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved sinterability.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. An ionic conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.3 to 1.7. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 10 mol%. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The total ionic conductivity is 0.28 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The solid electrolyte provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The tin substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tungsten stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 85%. The silicon substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the grain boundary resistance are improved.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing LiI. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12 and LiF present at grain boundaries. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1230 degrees C, and the resulting density is 92%. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium indium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium erbium bromide ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the solid-state battery. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The LATP and LLTO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Sintering at 1200 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP material. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the grain boundary resistance in contact with lithium.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP material. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the grain boundary resistance in contact with lithium.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. The LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and cycle life and rate capability.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 91% or more after sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a solid-state lithium battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.15 or less. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which solid electrolyte particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state lithium battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity of the layer.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6
abstract: Described is a lithium indium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 material. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium zirconate and to a method for producing the same. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium zirconate and to a method for producing the same. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LiF material. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% over 100 cycles. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the dendrite suppression is improved.

9. The method of claim 8, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.
10. The method of claim 8, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.
11. The method of claim 10, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
claims: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 25 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.
2. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 4.7 mol% to 6.8 mol%.
3. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 2, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.
4. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 3, wherein the reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the surface region.
5. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 1.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers.
6. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 90% or more.
7. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.8 V or more.

8. A method for producing the oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing lithium, titanium, hafnium, and phosphate sources at a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%; calcining the mixture at 700 degrees C to 900 degrees C; and sintering the calcined powder and forming the oxidation-resistant surface region by an oxygen anneal.
9. The method of claim 8, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
10. The method of claim 9, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.

11. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1.
12. The lithium secondary battery of claim 11, wherein the battery is pressed at a pressure of 1 MPa to 20 MPa during operation.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium yttrium chloride and to a method for producing the same. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the solid-state battery. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The content of GeS2 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. The roll temperature is 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers after calendering. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1230 degrees C, and the resulting density is 92%. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.075 or less. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. An ionic conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.1 to 0.55. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3YCl6. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3YCl6. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3BO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li2ZrO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and simpler handling.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with niobium and sintered with LiF is described. The Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a relative density of 97%. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.

The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved sinterability and high-voltage stability.
